title: Tandoori Chicken
summary: Chicken legs double-marinated in lemon and then a spiced yoghurt mix, roasted hot and finished under the grill for char, served with a fresh mint and coriander chutney.
equipment: roasting tin with a wire rack, lined with foil

ingredients.item: chicken legs (thighs and drumsticks), skin removed, slashed to the bone

ingredients.note: or 1½ tsp paprika + ½ tsp hot chilli powder

steps.title: Slash the chicken
steps.text: Cut 2-3 slashes through to the bone in each piece of chicken. This lets both marinades and the heat penetrate right through the meat rather than just seasoning the surface.

steps.title: First marinade
steps.text: Rub the chicken all over with the lemon juice and salt and leave for 20-30 minutes. The acid and salt begin seasoning the meat and help the thicker second marinade cling properly.

steps.title: Second marinade
steps.text: Mix the yoghurt with all the spices, ginger, garlic and oil, then coat the chicken thoroughly, working it into the slashes. Cover and refrigerate for 6-24 hours - the longer marinating time lets the spices and yoghurt's mild acidity tenderise the meat.

steps.title: Roast at high heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan) or its hottest setting, with a shelf in the top third. Lift the chicken from the marinade, letting the excess drip off, onto the rack in the roasting tin, and roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until the thigh reaches 80°C and the edges are browned.

steps.title: Char under the grill
steps.text: Finish the chicken under a high grill (broiler) for 3-5 minutes until charred in spots, or over high direct heat on a barbecue if you have one. This brief blast of fierce heat mimics the scorch of a tandoor without drying the meat out, since it's already cooked through.

steps.title: Make the chutney
steps.text: Blend the mint, coriander, chilli, lemon juice, yoghurt and salt until smooth.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the chicken with the onion rings, lemon wedges and chutney alongside.

tips: Don't skip the first lemon-and-salt marinade - it's what lets the thicker yoghurt marinade grip the meat properly.
Common mistake: roasting chicken skin-on for this dish. The skin is removed so the spiced yoghurt crust can form directly against the meat.
Letting excess marinade drip off before roasting stops the tin flooding with liquid and steaming the chicken instead of browning it.
A short blast under the grill at the end gives the char you'd get from a tandoor - don't be tempted to grill for longer, or the meat will dry out.
Make the chutney close to serving so the colour stays bright green.
storage: Store cooked chicken in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat until piping hot throughout (74°C) in an oven or under the grill rather than the microwave, which won't recreate the charred edges.
